absent: SCTP chunk and parameter header layouts, chunk type values and parameter type values are not shown.
SCTP association, transmission and congestion state machines, timer behavior and retransmission rules are not shown.
Locking, allocation, lifetime and concurrency rules for SCTP and LSM objects are not shown.
Capability helper internals, credential layout details and securebits mask values are not shown.
LSM dispatch when enabled, notifier payload contracts and mount-option handling are not shown.
File-identity list behind load-data enumeration and the unknown and maximum sentinel values are not shown.
Architecture-specific secure-boot override and integrity enforcement actions are not shown.

findings.text: Base SCTP operational error causes are 16-bit big-endian wire codes numbered from zero for no error upward through fourteen, covering stream validity, missing and invalid parameters, stale cookie, resource shortage, name resolution, unknown chunk, data availability, shutdown-cookie handling, plus restart, user abort, protocol violation and encapsulation-port renewal from the implementation guide.

Address reconfiguration acknowledgements use a higher range from 0xA0 through 0xA4 for last-address deletion, low resources, source-address deletion, illegal acknowledgement handling and refused authorization, while authenticated-chunk negotiation adds 0x105 for unsupported digest selection.

Congestion feedback centers on a 32-bit big-endian lowest unacknowledged marker called lowest_tsn; the ECNE wire form pairs a generic prologue chunk_hdr with a feedback member ence_hdr, while the CWR header carries the same marker shape without a chunk wrapper in these fragments.

Forward acknowledgement has classic and interleaved variants sharing a 32-bit big-endian new cumulative marker new_cum_tsn with an implied trailing skip array; classic skips pair stream with ssn, interleaved skips carry stream with reserved plus flags and mid, headers are named fwdtsn_hdr in both cases and each wire chunk prefixes its header with chunk_hdr.

Dynamic address signalling groups a parameter prologue param_hdr with a big-endian correlation value crr_id, a serial header serial with implied trailing parameters named addip_hdr, and a wire chunk that prefixes that header with chunk_hdr.

Authentication material pairs a key selector shkey_id with a digest selector hmac_id as big-endian 16-bit values plus implied trailing digest bytes under auth_hdr inside a chunk-prefixed container; a helper bundle joins an information pointer sctpinfo with an association pointer asoc; reconfiguration chunks carry only chunk_hdr plus implied trailing parameters.

Stream reset signalling uses parameter-prologued messages with big-endian sequence tracking under param_hdr: outgoing reset carries request_seq with response_seq plus send_reset_at_tsn and a trailing list_of_streams, incoming reset carries request_seq with trailing list_of_streams, timestamp reset carries only request_seq, stream addition carries request_seq with number_of_streams and reserved, and responses echo response_seq with result while the timestamp response also reports senders_next_tsn and receivers_next_tsn.

Reset outcomes are small host-order integers from zero for nothing to do through performed, denied, wrong sequence, concurrent operation, bad sequence number and in-progress states; separate masks isolate a set flag and value bits for differentiated-services handling and for flow-label handling with one set bit plus twenty value bits in the latter.

A reset exchange starts idle, may enter an in-progress condition when work remains, and then reaches one of performed, denied or error completions for wrong sequence, concurrent operation or bad numbering, after which a new sequence number begins another cycle.
Encapsulation-port renewal is a fixed parameter holding current port cur_port and replacement port new_port as two big-endian 16-bit values.
Length handling provides upward rounding to a four-byte boundary for padding and downward rounding to a four-byte boundary for truncation.
The secure-boot header defines a private inclusion marker and supplies a default architecture query for secure-boot state that reports disabled, leaving enabled platforms to override it.

The securebits header defines an inclusion marker set to one and exposes a predicate that tests whether a queried privilege bit is present by combining a mask helper for that bit with the current credential securebits field.
The security header defines a private inclusion marker to prevent repeated inclusion.
Capability option control uses zero for no options with distinct single-bit selections for suppressing audit and for set-identity context, and native label support is signalled by value one.

LSM notification distinguishes policy change from all-started conditions; a verity digest bundle joins an algorithm name alg with a byte string digest and its length digest_len; integrity classification separates verity signature validity from verity root hash and from fs-verity built-in signature validity.

Lockdown reasons form an ordered host enumeration beginning at unrestricted, proceeding through module, memory, firmware, execution, device-access, debug and tracing facilities, with two ceiling markers that split integrity restrictions from confidentiality restrictions and with the confidentiality ceiling closing the list.

Per-object LSM state aggregates four family members for SELinux selection and separately for Smack selection alongside AppArmor and BPF policy; transferable context carries a module-supplied string context with its length len and a numeric module identity id.
Both the enforced minimum mappable address and its discretionary default are zero in this configuration.

Set-identity categories use powers of two from one through eight for identity, real, saved and filesystem flavors; resource-limit mediation uses one for read and two for write; unsafe-clone annotations use one for shared state, two for traced ancestry and four for missing privilege-gain protection.

Extended-attribute initialization is a callback returning status for an inode; load-data identity builds an enumeration and a string table from a shared file-identity list, with enumeration names prefixed and string names plain, and a bounded identifier-to-string lookup that substitutes the unknown entry when the index reaches the maximum.

Property handling offers zeroing initialization, a populated test that compares against an empty value when enabled and a constant-false variant otherwise, plus blocking-notifier registration and dispatch that always succeed, name-to-attribute translation that always yields undefined, and an empty mount-option release.

Fallback hooks for initialization, binder mediation, quota, syslog, credentials, binary preparation, filesystem context, superblock and mount handling, path notification and most inode creation report success or do nothing, while process tracing, capability query and update, time setting, memory accounting and credential-from-file paths forward to capability or memory helpers, parameter parsing reports missing parameter and dentry security initialization reports unsupported operation.

Later inode hooks for link, unlink, symbolic link, directory creation, directory removal, device node, rename, readlink, link following, permission and attribute change uniformly report success, with temporary-file post-creation doing nothing.

Extended inode mediation for attribute query, access-control update and query with post notifications, extended-attribute query and listing with post notifications, file-attribute query and update, and privilege handling reports success or does nothing, while extended-attribute update and removal forward to capability helpers.

Fallback stubs are permissive by design and must not be mistaken for enforcement: most checks succeed silently, only narrow paths consult capability or memory helpers, two incompatible populated-test definitions coexist for different configurations, and the identifier-to-string helper masks out-of-range values as unknown rather than failing.
